   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 9pt;">&#xa0;</p></ix:exclude><ix:exclude></ix:exclude>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 9pt;"><i><b>Land&#xa0;Sales and Profit Recognition</b></i></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 9pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">In accordance with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">606,</em> land sales revenue is recognized when our performance obligations within the underlying sales contracts are fulfilled.&#xa0; The performance obligations in land sales contracts are typically satisfied at the point in time consideration&#xa0;and title is transferred through escrow at closing.&#xa0; Total revenue is typically recognized simultaneously with transfer of title to the customer.&#xa0; In instances where material performance obligations <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>exist after the closing date, a portion of the price is allocated to each performance obligation with revenue recognized as such obligations are completed.&#xa0; Variable consideration, such as profit participation, <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be included within the land sales transaction price based on the terms of a contract.&#xa0; The Company includes the estimated amount of variable consideration to which it will be entitled only to the extent it is probable that a significant reversal in the amount of cumulative revenue will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> occur when any uncertainty associated with the variable consideration is subsequently resolved.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 9pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 9pt;"><i><b>Fee Building</b></i></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">The Company enters into fee building agreements to provide services whereby it builds homes on behalf of <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party property owners. The <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party property owner funds all project costs incurred by the Company to build and sell the homes. The Company primarily enters into cost plus fee contracts where it charges <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party property owners for all direct and indirect costs plus a fee. The fee is typically a per-unit fixed fee or based on a percentage of the cost or home sales revenue of the project, depending on the terms of the agreement with the <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party property owner. For these types of contracts, the Company recognizes revenue based on the actual total costs it has incurred plus the applicable fee. In accordance with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">606,</em>&#xa0;we apply the percentage-of-completion method, using the cost-to-cost approach, as it most accurately measures the progress of our efforts in satisfying our obligations within the fee building agreements. Under this approach, revenue is earned in proportion to total costs incurred divided by total costs expected to be incurred. In the course of providing fee building services, the Company routinely subcontracts for services and incurs other direct costs on behalf of the property owners. These costs are passed through to the property owners and, in accordance with GAAP, are included in the Company&#x2019;s revenues and cost of sales.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">The Company also provides construction management and coordination services and sales and marketing services as part of agreements with <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> parties and its unconsolidated joint ventures. In certain contracts, the Company also provides project management and administrative services. For most services provided, the Company fulfills its related obligations as time-based measures, according to the input method guidance described in ASC <em style="font: inherit;">606.</em> Accordingly, revenue is recognized on a straight-line basis as the Company's efforts are expended evenly throughout the performance period. The Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>also have an obligation to manage the home or lot sales process as part of providing sales and marketing services. This obligation is considered fulfilled when related homes or lots close escrow, as these events represent milestones reached according to the output method guidance described in ASC <em style="font: inherit;">606.</em> Accordingly, revenue is recognized in the period that the corresponding lots or homes close escrow. Costs associated with these services are recognized as incurred.&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">The Company&#x2019;s fee building revenues have historically been concentrated with a small number of customers. For the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2019</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2018</em>, <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c68511639"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c68511935"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c68511936">one</span></span></span> customer comprise<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">d <ix:nonFraction id="c68511640" contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31_ConcentrationRiskByBenchmarkAxis-FeeBuildingRevenueMember_ConcentrationRiskByTypeAxis-CustomerConcentrationRiskMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskPercentage1" scale="-2" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="2">91</ix:nonFraction>%</span><span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">, <em style="font: inherit;">9</em></span><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c68511642">5%</span> and <ix:nonFraction id="c68511643" contextRef="d_2018-01-01_2018-12-31_ConcentrationRiskByBenchmarkAxis-FeeBuildingRevenueMember_ConcentrationRiskByTypeAxis-CustomerConcentrationRiskMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskPercentage1" scale="-2" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="2">95</ix:nonFraction>% of fee building revenue, respectively. The balance of the fee building revenues primarily represented fee billings from a new fee building arrangement and management fees earned from unconsolidated joint ventures and <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party customers. As of&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2019</em>, <em style="font: inherit;"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c68511937"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c68511938">one</span></span></em> customer comprised&#xa0;<ix:nonFraction id="c68511647" contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31_ConcentrationRiskByBenchmarkAxis-AccountsReceivableMember_ConcentrationRiskByTypeAxis-CustomerConcentrationRiskMember_MajorCustomersAxis-OneCustomerMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskPercentage1" scale="-2" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="2">35</ix:nonFraction>%&#xa0;and <ix:nonFraction id="c68511648" contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31_ConcentrationRiskByBenchmarkAxis-AccountsReceivableMember_ConcentrationRiskByTypeAxis-CustomerConcentrationRiskMember_MajorCustomersAxis-OneCustomerMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskPercentage1" scale="-2" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="2">65</ix:nonFraction>% of contracts and accounts receivable, respectively, and a separate fee building customer comprised <ix:nonFraction id="c68511649" contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31_ConcentrationRiskByBenchmarkAxis-AccountsReceivableMember_ConcentrationRiskByTypeAxis-CustomerConcentrationRiskMember_MajorCustomersAxis-SeparateFeeBuildingCustomerMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskPercentage1" scale="-2" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="2">25</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction id="c68511650" contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31_ConcentrationRiskByBenchmarkAxis-AccountsReceivableMember_ConcentrationRiskByTypeAxis-CustomerConcentrationRiskMember_MajorCustomersAxis-SeparateFeeBuildingCustomerMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskPercentage1" scale="-2" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3">0</ix:nonFraction>% of contracts and accounts receivable, respectively, with the balance of contracts and accounts receivable primarily representing escrow receivables from home sales.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0">&#xa0;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0"></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0"><b></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" name="us-gaap:ConsolidationVariableInterestEntityPolicy" id="c68518582" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0"><b>Variable Interest Entities</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">The Company accounts for variable interest entities in accordance with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">810,</em> <i>Consolidation</i> ("ASC <em style="font: inherit;">810"</em>). Under ASC <em style="font: inherit;">810,</em> a variable interest entity ("VIE") is created when: (a)&#xa0;the equity investment at risk in the entity is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> sufficient to permit the entity to finance its activities without additional subordinated financial support provided by other parties, including the equity holders; (b)&#xa0;the entity&#x2019;s equity holders as a group either (i)&#xa0;lack the direct or indirect ability to make decisions about the entity, (ii)&#xa0;are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> obligated to absorb expected losses of the entity or (iii)&#xa0;do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have the right to receive expected residual returns of the entity; or (c)&#xa0;the entity&#x2019;s equity holders have voting rights that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> proportionate to their economic interests, and the activities of the entity involve or are conducted on behalf of the equity holder with disproportionately few voting rights.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">Once we consider the sufficiency of equity and voting rights of each legal entity, we then evaluate the characteristics of the equity holders' interests, as a group, to see if they qualify as controlling financial interests. Our real estate joint ventures consist of limited partnerships and limited liability companies. For entities structured as limited partnerships or limited liability companies, our evaluation of whether the equity holders (equity partners other than us in each our joint ventures) lack the characteristics of a controlling financial interest includes the evaluation of whether the limited partners or non-managing members (the non-controlling equity holders) lack both substantive participating rights and substantive kick-out rights, defined as follows:</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#xa0;</p><ix:exclude><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"></p>

   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="width: 27pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">&#xa0;</td><td style="width: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#x2022;</p> </td><td style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Participating rights - provide the non-controlling equity holders the ability to direct significant financial and operational decision made in the ordinary course of business that most significantly influence the entity's economic performance.</p> </td></tr>

   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="width: 27pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">&#xa0;</td><td style="width: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#x2022;</p> </td><td style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">Kick-out rights - allow the non-controlling equity holders to remove the general partner or managing member without cause.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">If we conclude that any of the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> characteristics of a VIE are met, including if equity holders lack the characteristics of a controlling financial interest because they lack both substantive participating rights and substantive kick-out rights, we conclude that the entity is a VIE and evaluate it for consolidation under the variable interest model.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 24pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">If an entity is deemed to be a VIE pursuant to ASC <em style="font: inherit;">810,</em> the enterprise that has both (i)&#xa0;the power to direct the activities of a VIE that most significantly impact the entity&#x2019;s economic performance and (ii)&#xa0;the obligation to absorb the expected losses of the entity or right to receive benefits from the entity that could be potentially significant to the VIE is considered the primary beneficiary and must consolidate the VIE.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 24pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">Under ASC <em style="font: inherit;">810,</em> a nonrefundable deposit paid to an entity <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be deemed to be a variable interest that will absorb some or all of the entity&#x2019;s expected losses if they occur. Our land purchase and lot option deposits generally represent our maximum exposure to the land seller if we elect <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> to purchase the optioned property. In some instances, we <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>also expend funds for due diligence, development and construction activities with respect to optioned land prior to takedown. Such costs are classified as real estate inventories, which we would have to write off should we <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> exercise the option. Therefore, whenever we enter into a land option or purchase contract with an entity and make a nonrefundable deposit, a VIE <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>have been created.&#xa0;&#xa0;At <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020</em>, the Company had outstanding nonrefundable cash deposits of<span style="background-color:#ffffff;"> $<ix:nonFraction id="c68511666" contextRef="i_2020-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="nwhm:NonrefundableCashDeposits" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5">8.9</ix:nonFraction>&#xa0;milli</span>on&#xa0;pertaining to land option contracts and purchase contracts.<b>&#xa0; &#xa0;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 24pt;">As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2019</em>, the Company was <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> required to consolidate any VIEs. In accordance with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">810,</em> we perform ongoing reassessments of whether we are the primary beneficiary of a VIE.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 22.5pt;">&#xa0;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 22.5pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" name="us-gaap:ConsolidationSubsidiariesOrOtherInvestmentsConsolidatedEntitiesPolicy" id="c68518584" escape="true"><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b>Non-controlling Interest</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">During <em style="font: inherit;">2013,</em> the Company entered into a joint venture agreement with a <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party property owner. In accordance with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">810,</em> the Company analyzed this arrangement and determined that it was <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> a VIE; however, the Company determined it was required to consolidate the joint venture as the Company has a controlling financial interest with the powers to direct the major decisions of the entity.&#xa0; During <em style="font: inherit;">2020,</em> the Company and its partner dissolved the joint venture.&#xa0;&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#xa0;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" name="us-gaap:EquityMethodInvestmentsPolicy" id="c68518585" escape="true"><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b>Investments in and Advances to Unconsolidated Joint Ventures</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">We use the equity method to account for investments in homebuilding and land development joint ventures when any of the following situations exist: <em style="font: inherit;">1</em>) the joint venture qualifies as a VIE and we are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> the primary beneficiary, <em style="font: inherit;">2</em>) we do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> control the joint venture but have the ability to exercise significant influence over its operating and financial policies, or <em style="font: inherit;">3</em>) we function as the managing member or general partner of the joint venture and our joint venture partner has substantive participating rights or can replace us as managing member or general partner without cause.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">&#xa0;&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020</em>, the Company concluded that <em style="font: inherit;">none</em> of its joint ventures were VIEs and accounted for these entities under the equity method of accounting.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">Under the equity method, we recognize our proportionate share of earnings and losses generated by the joint venture upon the delivery of lots or homes to <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> parties. Our proportionate share of intra-entity profits and losses are eliminated until the related asset has been sold by the unconsolidated joint venture to <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> parties. We classify cash distributions received from equity method investees using the cumulative earnings approach consistent with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">230,</em>&#xa0;<i>Statement of Cash Flows </i>("ASC <em style="font: inherit;">230"</em>). Under the cumulative earnings approach, distributions received are considered returns on investment and are&#xa0;classified as cash inflows from operating activities unless the cumulative distributions received, less distributions received in prior periods that were determined to be returns of investment,&#xa0;exceed cumulative equity in earnings. When such an excess occurs, the current-period distribution up to this excess is considered a return of investment and is classified as cash inflows from investing activities. Our ownership interests in our unconsolidated joint ventures vary, but are generally less than or equal to <ix:nonFraction id="c68511687" contextRef="i_2020-12-31_RangeAxis-MaximumMember_ScheduleOfEquityMethodInvestmentEquityMethodInvesteeNameAxis-UnconsolidatedJointVenturesMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:EquityMethodInvestmentOwnershipPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="2">35</ix:nonFraction>%. The accounting policies of our joint ventures are consistent with those of the Company.&#xa0; &#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#xa0;</p><ix:exclude><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"></p>
   <div class="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-left: 0pt; margin-right: 0pt">
    <div class="PGNUM" style="text-align: center; width: 100%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">
     <em style="font: inherit;">76</em>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">We review real estate inventory held by our unconsolidated joint ventures for impairment on a quarterly basis, consistent with how we review our real estate inventories as described in more detail above in the section entitled "Real Estate Inventories and Cost of Sales." For the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2019</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2018</em>, our unconsolidated joint ventures recorded noncash impairment charges of $<ix:nonFraction id="c68511693" contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="nwhm:EquityMethodInvestmentImpairmentOfJointVentures" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3">0</ix:nonFraction>, $<ix:nonFraction id="c68511694" contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="nwhm:EquityMethodInvestmentImpairmentOfJointVentures" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-7">70.0</ix:nonFraction> million, and $<ix:nonFraction id="c68511695" contextRef="d_2018-01-01_2018-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="nwhm:EquityMethodInvestmentImpairmentOfJointVentures" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5">28.8</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively, of which $<ix:nonFraction id="c68511696" contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="nwhm:EquityMethodInvestmentImpairmentOfJointVentureAllocatedToCompany" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-3">0</ix:nonFraction>, $<ix:nonFraction id="c68511697" contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="nwhm:EquityMethodInvestmentImpairmentOfJointVentureAllocatedToCompany" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5">3.5</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c68511698" contextRef="d_2018-01-01_2018-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="nwhm:EquityMethodInvestmentImpairmentOfJointVentureAllocatedToCompany" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5">18.9</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively, was allocated to the Company. We also review our investments in and advances to unconsolidated joint ventures for evidence of other-than-temporary declines in value in accordance with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">820</em><i>.</i> To the extent we deem any portion of our investment in and advances to unconsolidated joint ventures as <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recoverable, we impair our investment accordingly.    <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#xa0;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" name="us-gaap:SellingGeneralAndAdministrativeExpensesPolicyTextBlock" id="c68518587" escape="true"><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b>Selling and Marketing Expense</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">Costs incurred for tangible assets directly used in the sales process such as our sales offices, design studios and model landscaping and furnishings are capitalized to other assets in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets under ASC <em style="font: inherit;">340,</em> <i>Other Assets and Deferred Costs</i> ("ASC <em style="font: inherit;">340"</em>). These costs are depreciated to selling and marketing expenses generally over the shorter of <em style="font: inherit;">30</em> months or the actual estimated life of the selling community. All other selling and marketing costs, such as commissions and advertising, are expensed as incurred.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#xa0;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" name="us-gaap:StandardProductWarrantyPolicy" id="c68518588" escape="true"><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b>Warranty and Litigation Accruals</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">We offer warranties on our homes that generally cover various defects in workmanship or materials, or structural construction defects for <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c68511709">one</span> year. In addition, we provide a more limited warranty, which generally ranges from a minimum of <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c68511710">two</span> years up to the period covered by the applicable statute of repose, that covers certain defined construction defects. Estimated future direct warranty costs are accrued and charged to cost of sales in the period when the related homebuilding revenues are recognized. Amounts are accrued based upon the Company&#x2019;s historical claim and expense&#xa0;rates. In addition, the Company has received warranty payments from <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party property owners for certain of its fee building projects that have since closed-out where the Company has the contractual risk of construction. These payments are recorded as warranty accruals. We assess the adequacy of our warranty accrual on a quarterly basis and adjust the amounts recorded if necessary. Our warranty accrual is included in accrued expenses and other liabilities in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets and adjustments to our warranty accrual are recorded through cost of sales or as an offset to warranty insurance receivables when covered by insurance.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">While our subcontractors who perform our homebuilding work generally provide us with an indemnity for claims relating to their workmanship and materials, we also purchase general liability insurance that covers development and construction activity at each of our communities. Our subcontractors are usually covered by these programs through an owner-controlled insurance program, or "OCIP." Consultants such as engineers and architects are generally <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> covered by the OCIP but are required to maintain their own insurance. In general, we maintain insurance, subject to deductibles and self-insured retentions, to protect us against various risks associated with our activities, including, among others, general liability, "all-risk" property, construction defects, workers&#x2019; compensation, automobile, and employee fidelity. Our master general liability policies which cover most of our projects allow for our warranty spend to erode our self-insured retention requirements. We establish a separate reserve for warranty and for known and incurred but <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> reported (&#x201c;IBNR&#x201d;) construction defect claims based on our historical claim and expense data. Our warranty accrual and litigation reserves for construction defect claims are presented on a gross basis within accrued expenses and other liabilities in our consolidated financial statements without consideration of insurance recoveries. Expected recoveries from insurance carriers are presented as warranty insurance receivables and insurance receivables within other assets in our consolidated balance sheets and are recorded based on actual insurance claims and amounts determined using our construction defect claim and warranty accrual estimates, our insurance policy coverage limits for the applicable policy years and historical recovery rates.&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&#xa0;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" name="us-gaap:ReceivablesPolicyTextBlock" id="c68518590" escape="true"><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b>Contracts and Accounts Receivable</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">Contracts and accounts receivable primarily represent the fees earned, but <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> collected, and reimbursable project costs incurred in connection with fee building agreements. The Company periodically evaluates the collectability of its contracts receivable, and, if it is determined that a receivable might <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be fully collectible, an allowance is recorded for the amount deemed uncollectible. This allowance for doubtful accounts is estimated based on management&#x2019;s evaluation of the contracts involved and the financial condition of its customers. Factors considered in such evaluations include, but are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> limited to: (i) customer type; (ii) historical contract performance; (iii) historical collection and delinquency trends; (iv) customer credit worthiness; and (v) general economic conditions. In addition to contracts receivable, escrow receivables are included in contracts and accounts receivable in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2019</em>, <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c68511719"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c68511939">no</span></span> allowance was recorded related to contracts and accounts receivable.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#xa0;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"></p><ix:exclude><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">&#xa0;</p>

   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#xa0;</p></ix:exclude><ix:exclude></ix:exclude>
   <p style="text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0"><b></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentPolicyTextBlock" id="c68518591" escape="true"><p style="text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0"><b>Property, Equipment and Capitalized Selling and Marketing Costs</b></p>
   <p style="text-indent: 27pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="text-indent: 27pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0">Property, equipment and capitalized selling and marketing costs are recorded at cost and included in other assets in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets. Property and equipment are depreciated to general and administrative expenses using the straight-line method over their estimated useful lives ranging from <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c68511723">three</span> to <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c68511724">five</span> years. Leasehold improvements are stated at cost and are amortized to general and administrative expenses using the straight-line method generally over the shorter of either their estimated useful lives or the term of the lease. Capitalized selling and marketing costs are depreciated using the straight-line method to selling and marketing expenses over the shorter of either <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" name="nwhm:CapitalizedSellingAndMarketingCostAmortizationPeriod" id="c68511725" format="ixt-sec:durmonth">30</ix:nonNumeric> months or the actual estimated life of the selling community. For the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2019</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2018</em>, the Company incurred depreciation and amortization expense<span style="background-color:#ffffff"> of $<ix:nonFraction id="c68511728" contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:Depreciation" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5">6.7</ix:nonFraction>&#xa0;million, $<ix:nonFraction id="c68511729" contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:Depreciation" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-6">9.0</ix:nonFraction>&#xa0;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c68511730" contextRef="d_2018-01-01_2018-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:Depreciation" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5">6.6</ix:nonFraction>&#xa0;million,&#xa0;respectively.&#xa0;</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0">&#xa0;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0"></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0"><b></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock" id="c68518592" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0"><b>Income Taxes</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">Income taxes are accounted for in accordance with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">740,</em> <i>Income Taxes</i> ("ASC <em style="font: inherit;">740"</em>). The consolidated provision for, or benefit from, income taxes is calculated using the asset and liability method, under which deferred tax assets and liabilities are recorded based on the difference between the financial statement and tax basis of assets and liabilities using enacted tax rates in effect for the year in which the differences are expected to reverse.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">Each quarter we assess our deferred tax asset to determine whether all or any portion of the asset is more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> (defined as a likelihood of more than <em style="font: inherit;">50%</em>) unrealizable under ASC <em style="font: inherit;">740.</em> We are required to establish a valuation allowance for any portion of the tax asset we conclude is more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> unrealizable. In accordance with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">740,</em> the determination of whether a valuation allowance for deferred tax assets is necessary requires an analysis of both positive and negative evidence regarding realization of the deferred tax assets and should be established based on the consideration of all available evidence. Our assessment considers, among other things, the nature, frequency and severity of prior cumulative losses, forecasts of future taxable income, the duration of statutory carryforward periods, our utilization experience with net operating losses and tax credit carryforwards and the available tax planning alternatives, to the extent these items are applicable, and the availability of net operating loss carrybacks under certain circumstances. The ultimate realization of deferred tax assets depends primarily on the generation of future taxable income during the periods in which the differences become deductible, as well as the ability to carryback net operating losses in the event that this option becomes available. The value of our deferred tax assets will depend on applicable income tax rates. Judgment is required in determining the future tax consequences of events that have been recognized in our consolidated financial statements and/or tax returns. Differences between anticipated and actual outcomes of these future tax consequences could have a material impact on our consolidated financial statements. At <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020, </em>based on our analysis of all available positive and negative evidence, and other relevant factors, we did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> establish a valuation allowance, except for $<ix:nonFraction id="c68511739" contextRef="i_2020-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">20,000</ix:nonFraction> related to a capital loss, and at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2019, </em><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c68511740">no</span> valuation allowance was recorded. Please refer to Note <em style="font: inherit;">14</em> for more information.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">ASC <em style="font: inherit;">740</em> defines the methodology for recognizing the benefits of uncertain tax return positions as well as guidance regarding the measurement of the resulting tax benefits. &#xa0;These provisions require an enterprise to recognize the financial statement effects of a tax position when it is more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not,</em> based on the technical merits, that the position will be sustained upon examination. &#xa0;In addition, these provisions provide guidance on derecognition, classification, interest and penalties, accounting in interim periods, disclosure, and transition. &#xa0;The evaluation of whether a tax position meets the more-likely-than-<em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recognition threshold requires a substantial degree of judgment by management based on the individual facts and circumstances. At <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020</em>, the Company has concluded that there were <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> significant uncertain tax positions requiring recognition in its financial statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">The Company classifies any interest and penalties related to income taxes assessed as part of income tax expense. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020</em>, the Company has <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c68511746">not</span> been assessed interest or penalties by any major tax jurisdictions related to any open tax periods.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#xa0;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationOptionAndIncentivePlansPolicy" id="c68518593" escape="true"><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b>Stock-Based&#xa0;Compensation</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">We account for share-based awards in accordance with ASC&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;">718,</em>&#xa0;<i>Compensation &#x2013; Stock Compensation</i>&#xa0;("ASC&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;">718"</em>) and ASC <em style="font: inherit;">505</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">50,</em> <i>Equity &#x2013; Equity Based Payments to Non-Employees</i>&#xa0;("ASC&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;">505</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">50"</em>).</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">ASC&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;">718</em> requires that the cost resulting from all share-based payment transactions be recognized in a company's financial statements. ASC&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;">718</em> requires all entities to apply a fair-value-based measurement method in accounting for share-based payment transactions with employees except for equity instruments held by employee share ownership plans.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> February 16, 2017, </em>the Company entered into an agreement that transitioned Wayne Stelmar's role within the Company from Chief Investment Officer to a non-employee consultant and non-employee director. Per the agreement, Mr. Stelmar's outstanding equity awards continued to vest in accordance with their original terms. Under ASC <em style="font: inherit;">505</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">50,</em> if an employee becomes a non-employee and continues to vest in an award pursuant to the award's original terms, that award will be treated as an award to a non-employee prospectively, provided the individual is required to continue providing services to the employer (such as consulting services).</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">&#xa0;</p><ix:exclude><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;"></p>
   <div class="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-left: 0pt; margin-right: 0pt">
    <div class="PGNUM" style="text-align: center; width: 100%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">
     <em style="font: inherit;">78</em>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">&#xa0;</p></ix:exclude><ix:exclude></ix:exclude>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">Based on the terms and conditions of Mr. Stelmar's consulting agreement&#xa0;noted above, we accounted for his&#xa0;share-based awards in accordance with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">505</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">50</em> through <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2018. </em>ASC&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;">505</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">50</em> required that these awards be accounted for prospectively, such that the fair value of the awards was re-measured at each reporting date until the earlier of (a) the performance commitment date or (b) the date the services required under the transition agreement with Mr. Stelmar have been completed. ASC <em style="font: inherit;">505</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">50</em> required that compensation cost ultimately recognized in the Company's financial statements be the sum of (a) the compensation cost recognized during the period of time the individual was an employee (based on the grant-date fair value) plus (b) the fair value of the award determined on the measurement date determined in accordance with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">505</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">50</em> for the pro-rata portion of the vesting period in which the individual was a non-employee.&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> June </em>of <em style="font: inherit;">2018,</em> the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2018</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">07,</em><i> Improvements to Nonemployee Share-Based Payment Accounting</i> ("ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2018</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">07"</em>) which expanded the scope of ASC <em style="font: inherit;">718</em> to include share-based payments for acquiring goods and services from nonemployees, with certain exceptions. Under ASC <em style="font: inherit;">718,</em> the measurement date for equity-classified, share-based awards is generally the grant date of the award. The Company early adopted ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2018</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">07</em> on <em style="font: inherit;"> April 1, 2018, </em>at which time Mr. Stelmar's award was the only nonemployee award outstanding. In accordance with the transition guidance, the Company assessed Mr. Stelmar's award for which a measurement date had <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> been established. The outstanding award was re-measured to fair value as of the <em style="font: inherit;"> April 1, 2018 </em>adoption date. The adoption of ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2018</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">07</em> provided&#xa0;administrative relief by fixing the remaining unamortized expense of the award and eliminating the requirement to quarterly re-measure the Company's <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> remaining nonemployee award. The Company adopted this standard on a modified retrospective basis booking a cumulative-effect adjustment of an $<ix:nonFraction id="c68511786" contextRef="i_2018-01-01_AdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis-AccountingStandardsUpdate201807Member_CumulativeEffectPeriodOfAdoptionAxis-CumulativeEffectPeriodOfAdoptionAdjustmentMember_StatementEquityComponentsAxis-RetainedEarningsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:StockholdersEquityIncludingPortionAttributableToNoncontrollingInterest" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">18,000</ix:nonFraction> increase to retained earnings and equal decrease to additional paid-in capital as of the beginning of the <em style="font: inherit;">2018</em> fiscal year. Mr. Stelmar's award was fully expensed as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March&#xa0;</em><em style="font: inherit;">31,</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2019.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#xa0;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" name="us-gaap:StockholdersEquityPolicyTextBlock" id="c68518594" escape="true"><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b>Share Repurchase and Retirement</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 22.5pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">When shares are retired, the Company&#x2019;s policy is to allocate the excess of the repurchase price over the par value of shares acquired to both retained earnings and additional paid-in capital. The portion allocated to additional paid-in capital is determined by applying a percentage, which is determined by dividing the number of shares to be retired by the number of shares issued, to the balance of additional paid-in capital as of the retirement date. The residual, if any, is allocated to retained earnings as of the retirement date.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 22.5pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">During the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020</em>, the Company repurchased and retired <ix:nonFraction id="c68511790" contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockRepurchasedAndRetiredDuringPeriodShares" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">2,160,792</ix:nonFraction> shares of its common stock at an aggregate purchase price <span style="background-color:#ffffff;">of $<ix:nonFraction id="c68511791" contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:StockRepurchasedAndRetiredDuringPeriodValue" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5">4.3</ix:nonFraction></span><span style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#xa0;m</span>illion.&#xa0; During the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2019, </em>the Company repurchased and retired <ix:nonFraction id="c68511792" contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockRepurchasedAndRetiredDuringPeriodShares" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">153,916</ix:nonFraction> shares of its common stock at an aggregate purchase price of $<ix:nonFraction id="c68511794" contextRef="d_2019-01-01_2019-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:StockRepurchasedAndRetiredDuringPeriodValue" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-6">1.0</ix:nonFraction>&#xa0;million.&#xa0; During the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2018,&#xa0;</em>the Company repurchased and retired <ix:nonFraction id="c68511795" contextRef="d_2018-01-01_2018-12-31" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockRepurchasedAndRetiredDuringPeriodShares" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">1,003,116</ix:nonFraction> shares of its common stock at an aggregate purchase price of $<ix:nonFraction id="c68511796" contextRef="d_2018-01-01_2018-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="nwhm:StockRepurchasedAndRetiredDuringPeriodLessCommissionsValue" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5">8.5</ix:nonFraction> million&#xa0;&#xa0;All repurchased shares were returned to the status of authorized but unissued.&#xa0; All purchases were made under a previously announced repurchase program that had a remaining authorization of $<ix:nonFraction id="c68511797" contextRef="i_2020-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:StockRepurchaseProgramRemainingAuthorizedRepurchaseAmount1" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5">9.4</ix:nonFraction> million at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020.&#xa0;</em></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#xa0;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" name="nwhm:TaxBenefitPreservationPlanPolicyTextBlock" id="c68518595" escape="true"><p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>Tax Benefit Preservation Plan</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> May 8, 2020, </em>the Company entered into a Tax Benefit Preservation Plan between the Company and American Stock Transfer &amp; Trust Company, LLC, as rights agent (as amended from time to time, the &#x201c;Tax Plan&#x201d;) to help preserve the value of certain deferred tax benefits, including those generated by net operating losses and certain other tax attributes (collectively, the &#x201c;Tax Benefits&#x201d;). The Tax Plan is intended to act as a deterrent to any person or entity acquiring shares of the Company equal to or exceeding <em style="font: inherit;">4.95%.</em> The Tax Plan reduces the likelihood that changes in our investor base have the unintended effect of limiting the use of our Tax Benefits. In connection with its adoption of the Tax Plan, the Board declared a dividend of <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c68511799">one</span> preferred stock purchase right (individually, a &#x201c;Right&#x201d; and collectively, the &#x201c;Rights&#x201d;) for each share of Common Stock, par value $<ix:nonFraction id="c68511800" contextRef="i_2020-05-08" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:CommonStockParOrStatedValuePerShare" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">0.01</ix:nonFraction> (&#x201c;Common Stock&#x201d;) of the Company outstanding at the close of business on <em style="font: inherit;"> May 20, 2020.&#xa0; </em>As long as the Rights are attached to the Common Stock, the Company will issue <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> Right (subject to adjustment) with each new share of the Common Stock so that all such shares will have attached Rights.&#xa0; Each Right has an exercise price of $<ix:nonFraction id="c68511802" contextRef="i_2020-05-08" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="nwhm:PreferredStockPurchaseRightExercisePrice" scale="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF">11.50</ix:nonFraction>. Each Right, which is only exercisable if a person or group of affiliated or associated persons acquires beneficial ownership of <em style="font: inherit;">4.95%</em> or more of the Common Stock, subject to certain limited exceptions (the &#x201c;Acquiring Person&#x201d;), when exercised will entitle the registered holder other than the Acquiring Person the right to acquire <em style="font: inherit;">1/1000</em><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:pt">th</sup> of a share of our Series A Junior Participating Preferred Stock.&#xa0; In addition, in certain circumstances, each registered holder will have the right to receive upon exercise, that number of shares of Common Stock having a market value of <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> times the <em style="font: inherit;">$11.50</em> exercise price of the Right, or, at the election of the Board, to exchange each right for <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> share of Common Stock, in each case, subject to adjustment. Unless redeemed&#xa0;or exchanged earlier by the Company or terminated, the rights will expire upon the earliest to occur of (i) the close of business on <em style="font: inherit;"> May 7, 2021, (</em>ii) the close of business on the effective date of the repeal of Section <em style="font: inherit;">382</em> of the Internal Revenue Code of <em style="font: inherit;">1986,</em> as amended (the &#x201c;Code&#x201d;) if the Board determines that the Tax Plan is <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> longer necessary or desirable for the preservation of the Tax Benefits or (iii) the time at which the Board determines that the Tax Benefits are fully utilized or <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> longer available under Section <em style="font: inherit;">382</em> of the Code or that an ownership change under Section <em style="font: inherit;">382</em> of the Code would <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> adversely impact in any material respect the time period in which the Company could use the Tax Benefits, or materially impair the amount of the Tax Benefits that could be used by the Company in any particular time period, for applicable tax purposes.&#xa0;</p>

We currently intend to retain our future earnings to finance the development and expansion of our business and, therefore, do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> intend to pay cash dividends on our common stock for the foreseeable future. Any future determination to pay dividends will be at the discretion of our board of directors and will depend on our financial condition, results of operations, capital requirements, compliance with Delaware law, restrictions contained in any financing instruments, including but <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> limited to, our unsecured credit facility and senior notes indenture, and such other factors as our board of directors deem relevant.</p>

     $<ix:nonFraction id="c68511834" contextRef="d_2018-01-01_2018-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanEmployerDiscretionaryContributionAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-6">1.0</ix:nonFraction>&#xa0;million, respectively.

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0">&#xa0;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0"></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c68518598" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b><span style="background-color:#ffffff">Recently Issued Accounting Standards</span></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">In&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 2016,&#xa0;</em>the FASB issued ASU&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;">2016</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">13</em><i>,</i>&#xa0;<i>Financial Instruments - Credit Losses (Topic&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;">326</em>) - Measurement of Credit Losses on Financial Instruments&#xa0;</i>("ASU&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;">2016</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">13</em><i>"</i>), which changes the impairment model for most financial assets and certain other instruments from an "incurred loss" approach to a new "expected credit loss" methodology. The FASB followed up with ASU&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;">2019</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">04</em><i>,</i>&#xa0;<i>Codification Improvements to Topic&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;">326,</em>&#xa0;Financial Instruments - Credit Losses, Topic&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;">815,</em>&#xa0;Derivatives and Hedging, and Topic&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;">825,</em>&#xa0;Financial Instruments</i>&#xa0;in&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;"> April 2019,&#xa0;</em>ASU&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;">2019</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">05</em><i>,</i>&#xa0;<i>Financial Instruments - Credit Losses (Topic&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;">326</em>)</i>&#xa0;in&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;"> May 2019, </em>ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2019</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">11,</em> <i>Codification Improvements to Topic <em style="font: inherit;">326,</em> Financial Instruments - Credit Losses </i>in <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2019, </em>a<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">nd ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2020</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">02,</em> <i>Financial Instruments - Credit Losses (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">326</em>) and Leases (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">842</em>) </i>in <em style="font: inherit;"> February 2020&#xa0;</em>to provide further clarification on this topic. The standard is effective for annual and interim periods beginning&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2020</em></span><i><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">,&#xa0;</span></i><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">and requires full retrospective application upon adoption.&#xa0; During <em style="font: inherit;"> November&#xa0;</em><em style="font: inherit;">2019</em></span><i><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">,&#xa0;</span></i><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">the FASB issued ASU&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;">2019</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10</em></span><i><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">,</span></i><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">&#xa0;</span><i><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">Financial Instruments - Credit Losses&#xa0;(Topic <em style="font: inherit;">326</em>),&#xa0;Derivatives and Hedging (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">815</em>) and Leases (Topic&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;">842</em>) Effective Dates </span></i><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">that</span><i><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">&#xa0;</span></i><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">provides for</span><i><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">&#xa0;</span></i><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">additional implementation time for smaller repor</span>ting companies with the standard being effective for smaller reporting companies for&#xa0;fiscal years beginning after&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2022</em><i>,&#xa0;</i>including interim periods within those fiscal years.&#xa0; Early adoption is permitted.&#xa0; As a smaller reporting company, we did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> adopt&#xa0;the requirements of ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2016</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">13</em>&#xa0;for the year beginning <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1,&#xa0;</em><em style="font: inherit;">2020,</em> however we do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#xa0;anticipate a material impact to our&#xa0;consolidated financial statements as a result of adoption.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> August 2018, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2018</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">13,</em> <i>Fair Value Measurement (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">820</em>) - Disclosure Framework - Changes to the Disclosure Requirements for Fair Value Measurement </i>("ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2018</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">13"</em>). The amendments in ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2018</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">13</em> modify certain disclosure requirements of fair value measurements.&#xa0; The Company adopted ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2018</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">13</em> effective <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2020 </em>and experienced <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> impact to the consolidated financial statements as a result of adoption.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2019, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2019</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">12,</em> <i>Income Taxes (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">740</em>)-</i>&#xa0;<i>Simplifying the Accounting for Income Taxes </i>("ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2019</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">12"</em>),&#xa0;which is intended to simplify various aspects related to accounting for income taxes. The pronouncement is effective for fiscal years, and for interim periods within those fiscal years, beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2020, </em>with early adoption permitted.&#xa0; We did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> early-adopt ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2019</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">12</em> and are currently in the process of evaluating the effects on our financial statements of its adoption.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;"><span style="background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> January 2020, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2020</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">01,</em> </span><i><span style="background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">Investments - Equity Securities (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">321</em>), Investments - Equity Method and Joint Ventures (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">323</em>), and Derivative and Hedging (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">815</em>)</span></i><span style="background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"> ("ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2020</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">01"</em>).&#xa0; ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2020</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">01</em> clarifies&#xa0;the interaction of the accounting for equity securities under Topic <em style="font: inherit;">321</em> and investments accounted for under the equity method of accounting in Topic <em style="font: inherit;">323</em> and the accounting for certain forward contracts and purchased options accounted for under Topic <em style="font: inherit;">815.</em>&#xa0; The standard is effective for fiscal years beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020, </em>and interim periods within those fiscal years, with early adoption permitted.&#xa0; The Company is currently evaluating ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2020</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">01</em> and expects <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> material impact to our consolidated financial&#xa0;statements as a result of adoption.&#xa0;&#xa0;</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> March 2020, </em>the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) adopted amendments to the financial disclosure requirements applicable to registered debt offerings that include credit enhancements, such as subsidiary guarantees, in Rule <em style="font: inherit;">3</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10</em> of Regulation S-<em style="font: inherit;">X.</em> The amended rule focuses on providing material, relevant and decision-useful information regarding guarantees and other credit enhancements, while eliminating certain prescriptive requirements. The Company adopted these amendments for the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020 </em>with <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> impact to our consolidated financial statements and related disclosures.&#xa0; In <em style="font: inherit;"> October 2020, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2020</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09,</em> <i>Debt (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">470</em>) - Amendments to SEC Paragraphs Pursuant to SEC Release <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">33</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10762</em> </i>("ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2020</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09"</em><i>)</i>&#xa0;to reflect the SEC&#x2019;s new disclosure rules on guaranteed debt securities.&#xa0;&#xa0;</p>

The amendments in ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2020</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10</em> contain improvements to the Codification by including disclosure guidance in appropriate disclosure and ensuring that all guidance that requires or provides an option for an entity to provide information in the notes to financial statements is codified in the Disclosure Section of the Codification.    <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;text-indent:27pt;">In accordance with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">360,</em> inventory is stated at cost, unless the carrying amount is determined <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> to be recoverable, in which case inventory is written down to its fair value. We review each real estate asset at the community-level on a quarterly basis or whenever indicators of impairment exist. Due to the lower demand levels experienced at this community coupled with the substantial investment required to build out the remainder of the project, the Company decided to abandon the future acquisition, development, construction and sale of future phases of the project that were under option.&#xa0;In accordance with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">970</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">360</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">40</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">1,</em> the capitalized costs related to the project are expensed and <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> allocated to other components of the project that the Company did develop. For the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020,&#xa0;</em>the Company recorded an abandonment charge of $<ix:nonFraction id="c68512136" contextRef="d_2020-01-01_2020-12-31_RealEstateAndAccumulatedDepreciationDescriptionOfPropertyAxis-LuxuryCondominiumProjectInScottsdaleArizonaMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfLongLivedAssetsToBeDisposedOf" scale="6" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-6">14.0</ix:nonFraction> million representing the capitalized costs that have accumulated related to the portion of the project that is being abandoned.&#xa0; This charge is&#xa0;included within project abandonment costs in the accompanying consolidated statement of operations.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">5.</em>&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;&#xa0;Capitalized Interest</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#xa0;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 27pt;">Interest is capitalized to inventory and investment in unconsolidated joint ventures during development and other qualifying activities. Interest capitalized as a cost of inventory is included in cost of sales as related homes and land parcels are closed. Interest capitalized to investment in unconsolidated joint ventures is amortized to equity in net income (loss) of unconsolidated joint ventures as related joint venture homes or lots close, or in instances where lots are sold from the unconsolidated joint venture to the Company, the interest is added to the land basis and included in cost of sales when the related lots or homes are sold to <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party buyers.&#xa0; Interest expense is comprised of interest incurred but&#xa0;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em> capitalized and is reported as interest expense in our consolidated statements of operations.&#xa0; For the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2020, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2019</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2018</em> interest incurred, capitalized and expensed was as follows:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;text-indent:27pt;">&#xa0;</p>
